listen.explanationKey: What is one way Americans can serve their country?
facts: Americans can serve their country in many ways: vote, pay taxes, obey the law, serve in the military, run for office or work for the government.
Civic participation means taking part in your community and government.
Voting, joining a community group, helping with a campaign and contacting elected officials are all civic participation.

newWords.meaning: to do work that helps others
taking part in your community and government
the work to help someone win an election
serving on a jury when a court calls you

story.say: Americans can serve their country in many ways.

help.simpler: There are many ways to help your country.
help.example: Some are things people do every day, like obeying the law.
help.why: The test asks for one way Americans can serve their country.

story.say: They can vote, pay taxes and obey the law.

help.simpler: Voting, paying taxes and following the law all help the country.
help.example: Taxes help pay for roads, schools and the military.
help.why: Any one of these is an answer on the test.

story.say: They can serve in the military, run for office or work for the government.

help.simpler: Some people serve by joining the military, running for office or working for the government.
help.example: A park ranger works for the government.
help.why: These are more answers for how Americans serve their country.

check.prompt: Tap the way to serve that means following the rules.

story.say: Civic participation means taking part in your community and government.

help.example: Going to a town meeting is civic participation.
help.why: The test asks for two examples of civic participation.

story.say: Voting and joining a community group are civic participation.

help.simpler: Voting is taking part. So is joining a group that helps your community.
help.example: A neighborhood clean-up group is a community group.
help.why: “Vote” and “Join a community group” are two answers on the test.

story.say: So are helping with a campaign and contacting your elected officials.

help.simpler: Helping someone run for office, or telling leaders your opinion, also counts.
help.example: You can call or write to your representative about an issue you care about.
help.why: “Help with a campaign” and “Give an elected official your opinion” are more answers.

check.prompt: Which one is an example of civic participation?

readIt.sentence: What can people do for the country?

listen.explanationKey: Why is it important to pay federal taxes?
facts: Paying federal taxes is required by law. All people pay to fund the federal government.
The Constitution's 16th Amendment lets Congress collect a federal income tax.
Men age 18 through 25 register for the Selective Service. It is required by law, and it makes a draft fair if one is ever needed.

newWords.meaning: to put your name on an official list
when the government calls people to serve in the military
money you pay the government from what you earn
the list where men 18 to 25 register in case of a draft for the military. All men must put their name in case the United States goes to war.

story.say: Paying federal taxes is required by law.

help.simpler: The law says people must pay federal taxes.
help.example: Many workers pay taxes from each paycheck.
help.why: “Required by law” is one answer to why paying federal taxes is important.

story.say: All people pay to fund the federal government.

help.simpler: Tax money pays for the government’s work.
help.example: Taxes help pay for national parks, the military and highways.
help.why: “All people pay to fund the federal government” is another answer.

check.statement: Paying federal taxes is required by law.

story.say: The Constitution’s 16th Amendment lets Congress collect a federal income tax.

help.simpler: The 16th Amendment allows a tax on income, the money people earn.
help.example: It was added to the Constitution in 1913.
help.why: “Required by the Constitution (16th Amendment)” is another answer on the test.

story.say: Men age 18 through 25 register for the Selective Service.

help.simpler: Young men from age 18 through 25 sign up with the Selective Service.
help.example: This picture shows men who had just registered in 1917, during World War I.
help.why: The test asks you to name one reason this registration is important.

check.prompt: Who registers for the Selective Service?

help.simpler: The law says men in this age group must register.
help.example: Registering means giving your name and address to the Selective Service.
help.why: “Required by law” is one answer on the test.

story.say: And it makes a draft fair, if one is ever needed.

help.simpler: If the country ever needs more soldiers, a draft would choose fairly from the list.
help.example: “Draft” means the government calls people to serve in the military.
help.why: “Makes the draft fair, if needed” is another answer on the test.

check.statement: Registering for the Selective Service is required by law.

readIt.sentence: Why do we pay for the government?
